walkthroughs.body_html:
Use of Biological Resources — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Use of Biological Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Use of Biological Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.

mcqs.q: How do decomposers return carbon to the atmosphere?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Decomposers turn dead matter into oxygen and water, with no carbon involved.
They respire — breaking down dead organic matter and releasing CO2.
Decomposers release carbon by physically breaking matter into smaller pieces.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?

Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: In a fermenter producing yoghurt, microorganisms are grown at a controlled temperature. Why is temperature carefully controlled?
options: To keep enzymes at their optimum without denaturing them
To kill all the microorganisms
To stop respiration completely
To remove all oxygen

mcqs.q: Selective breeding of crops for high yield over many generations can reduce genetic variation. Why is low variation a risk?
options: The whole crop may be vulnerable to the same disease.
The crop will grow more slowly each year.
The crop becomes a different species.
Low variation always increases yield.

mcqs.q: Fish farming often keeps predators away and controls food supply. The main aim of these measures is to:
options: Increase the number and growth of fish produced
Reduce the energy the fish receive
Encourage more competition between fish
Lower the water oxygen level

mcqs.q: Yeast is used to make bread rise. Which product of anaerobic respiration in yeast causes the dough to rise?
options: Carbon dioxide
Lactic acid
Oxygen
Glucose
